reason: The text explicitly depicts non-leader agents exercising agency. Most notably, Rahab (a prostitute, not a leader) actively hides the spies and negotiates the safety of her family (וְהֶחְבִּיאָה אֶת־ הַמַּלְאָכִים 'she hid the messengers'). The two spies, who are not authority figures, conduct reconnaissance and move independently. Additionally, while the common people receive explicit orders limiting their speech (לֹא תָרִיעוּ 'you shall not shout'), they still exercise agency in participating in the march and eventually shouting when commanded. Agency is demonstrated across hierarchies, not confined to leaders alone.
